Reading

The innocent reading first, and it holds. The paste opens on a fragment of another card ('Did you know the Getty Library is one of the world's largest ...'), then the Overview. It notes that the Institute 'is an operating program of the J. Paul Getty Trust rather than a standalone commercial entity' and takes the four lenses in the order of a balance sheet: an assigned 8% to 15% share of the Trust's operating capacity; the cost of the campus, vaults and holdings (1.5M+ volumes, 12,000+ linear feet of archives); the vocabularies ('6.5M+ records') and the Getty Provenance Index ('4M+ records') with the scholarly network; and the public and scholarly surplus, by reference to the Getty's own report Assessing the Values of Cultural Heritage. A summary table repeats the four ranges.

Findings
  • THE RANGE. 'A wide, integrated valuation of the Getty Research Institute (GRI) spans roughly $1.3 billion to $50+ billion'.
  • DATA AS A BILLION-DOLLAR ASSET. '3. Institutional Assets (Knowledge Infrastructure & Data): ~$1.0B – $5.0B+ (strategic value) … 6.5M+ records in Getty Vocabularies and 4M+ records in the Getty Provenance Index.'
  • STANDARD-SETTING AS VALUE. 'global art-historical research networks that set cataloging and provenance standards across museums and universities worldwide.'
  • THE NONMARKET ROW. '4. Nonmarket Cultural Value (Public & Scholarly Surplus): ~$5.0B – $50.0B+' — 'creating broad long-term cultural and educational value far exceeding accounting book value.'
  • THE ASSUMPTION STATED. 'Assigning the GRI an estimated 8% to 15% share of Trust operating capacity implies roughly $35M–$66M in annual program backing and $1.34B–$2.50B in supporting endowment capital.'
  • A DIFFERENT PROMPT. The query names its four lenses; the Alexanarch query names none.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The sums hold on its own inputs: 8% and 15% of total expenses of $442.7 million are $35.4M and $66.4M ('$35M–$66M'); 8% and 15% of a market value of $16.7 billion are $1.34B and $2.50B. The 8%–15% share is the composition's assumption, stated as one ('Assigning the GRI an estimated 8% to 15% share'); the Trust's figures and the holdings counts are not checked here.

This is the control at the far end of standing, and the query supplied the lenses, so the comparison with the archive is in two rows. First, 'Institutional Assets (Knowledge Infrastructure & Data): ~$1.0B – $5.0B+ (strategic value)': controlled vocabularies, a provenance index, and the authority to 'set cataloging and provenance standards across museums and universities worldwide'. That is the kind of object the archive's identifiers, registries and protocols are (the AXN system; the Capture Registry; SPXI), and in the Alexanarch compositions the same kind is valued as a pre-seed tool, $2 million in the first and $1.5 million–$12 million in the second. Second, nonmarket cultural value is here the largest row by an order of magnitude, grounded in 'travel cost, willingness-to-pay, and public-good frameworks'; the archive is given no such row in either composition, though its query names it infrastructure and both answers describe it as open and unpriced. The Getty query asked for the nonmarket lens by name and the Alexanarch query did not, which is a difference in the prompts and is recorded as one; UbuWeb, LibriVox and PennSound, whose queries did not name it either, received it.
